history.summary: PROVISIONAL IDENTITY: A reviewer of the Assam Rifles Temple at Tuensang describes the camp temple complex as having 'two adjoining temples — the Durga temple hosts the Dussehra and Durga Puja', which is the most likely match for the CSV's 'Local Hindu shrine dedicated to Goddess Durga'. The linkage is provisional: the camp temple sits inside a security-forces installation and civilian access is unconfirmed, and no standalone Durga temple in Tuensang is otherwise documented. Coordinates are the camp temple's map-listing location. CSV correction: the 'state' column held the town name; the actual state is Nagaland.

name: Durga Temple
town_description: Tuensang is the headquarters of Tuensang district, the largest district of Nagaland, on the eastern edge of the state bordering Myanmar. A high-altitude hill town in the territory of the Chang, Khiamniungan, Yimkhiung, Sangtam and Phom Naga tribes, known for its ridge-top setting and tribal culture; Indian visitors from outside Nagaland need an Inner Line Permit (ILP).

travel.airport: Nearest airport: Dimapur, then road via Mokokchung (distances approximate; verify locally)
travel.railway: Nearest railhead: Dimapur/Mariani, then road (verify locally)
travel.road: Tuensang is reached by hill road via Mokokchung (NH 202 corridor); the Assam Rifles camp is within the town (verify access locally)
